name: Incuca Intelligence
author: Incuca

sections.description:
Incuca Intelligence measures the visits to your site and shows them next to your other numbers in your Incuca Intelligence account.

This plugin adds the measurement tag to the header of every page. It does not add pages and does not store anything about your visitors in your WordPress database.

If the owner of the Incuca Intelligence account turns on a text test (A/B test), the tag can swap the text of some elements on the page for part of the visitors. Without a test turned on, the tag does not change the page.

You need an Incuca Intelligence account. The plugin does nothing until a site key is set. If you downloaded the plugin from your account, the key is already inside the file. Otherwise, open Settings, Incuca Intelligence, and click “Connect to Intelligence”: you approve the site in your account and come back connected, without copying the key. You can also paste the key there. The plugin keeps the key in one WordPress option, so it survives updates.

The tag is added once per page by this plugin.

External services

This plugin loads a script from the Incuca Intelligence service. The script runs in the browser of each visitor and sends the data listed below to the service, so that your account can count it.

  • Service: Incuca Intelligence, provided by Incuca.
  • When: every time a visitor opens a page of your site, once the site key is set. On sites that change pages without reloading, each change of page counts as a visit.
  • Sent with every visit: the page path and title, the site address, the referrer, the width of the window, whether the page is where the visit began, the site key, and the visitor’s IP address (sent with the request). The service also reads the browser, the system and the type of device from the browser’s identification.
  • Sent when the visit comes from a campaign link or from an ad: the campaign source, medium and name, and whether the ad is from Google or Microsoft. The ad click code itself is not sent.
  • Sent as events: a form that was submitted (never what was typed), a click on a WhatsApp link, a click on a phone link, and goals that the site itself declares.
  • Sent for speed: how long the page took to respond to the visitor’s clicks and taps.
  • Sent for text tests: which version of the test (A or B) the visitor saw. The browser keeps this choice for the session.
  • Terms of use: https://incuca.net/termos-de-uso/
  • Privacy notice: https://incuca.net/aviso-de-privacidade/

Connecting the site is the only time your server contacts the service, and it only happens after an administrator clicks “Connect to Intelligence”:

  • What happens: the click opens your Incuca Intelligence account in the browser, where you approve the site. The service sends the browser back to this settings page with a one-time code, valid for 15 minutes. Your server then sends one request to the service, over HTTPS with the certificate checked, and receives the site key.
  • Sent in that request: the one-time code and the address of your WordPress. Nothing about your visitors, your users or your content is sent.
  • Address: https://api-insights.incuca.net/api/v1/wordpress/conexao/troca
  • The click is the consent. Without it, your server does not contact the service. Disconnecting removes the key from this site.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress, open Plugins, then Add New, then Upload Plugin.
  2. Choose the file and click Activate.
  3. If the plugin came without a key, open Settings, then Incuca Intelligence, and click “Connect to Intelligence”. You can also paste the site key there and save.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin work without an account?

No. The tag only counts visits for a site registered in an Incuca Intelligence account.

Does the plugin slow my site down?

The script loads asynchronously, so it does not block the page from showing.

How do I remove it?

Deactivate and delete the plugin. The saved key is removed with it.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • “Connect to Intelligence” button: connects the site without copying the key.
  • Disconnect button.
  • Portuguese and Spanish translations included (WordPress 6.5 or later; older versions show English).

1.0.0

  • First version.
